question: How do the frozen trend-direction descriptor and the two frozen breadth descriptors relate contemporaneously across indices, market views, years, and state transitions?
purpose: Outcome-blind state redundancy and geometry only.
forbidden_inputs: strategy membership, trades, returns, P&L, MFE, MAE, exits, duration, or outcome class

trend_panel.representation: direction_return_60 and its causal PIT coordinates only

fixed_geometry.continuous: Spearman association for each of 6 index x 4 breadth-view pairs; median/range only, not pooled independent inference
fixed_geometry.conditional: rank-residual discovery-versus-concentration association controlling contemporaneous direction
fixed_geometry.direction_state: POSITIVE if absolute 60-session log direction >0; NEGATIVE if <0; exact zero is NEUTRAL
fixed_geometry.discovery_state: EXPANSION if net new-high/new-low participation >0; BREAKDOWN if <0; exact zero is BALANCED
fixed_geometry.concentration_state: CONCENTRATED if causal 3-year percentile >=0.80; DIFFUSE if <=0.20; otherwise MIDDLE
fixed_geometry.transition: descriptive next-session state transition and dwell time; never a forecast or action rule

representation_gate.trend_breadth_nonredundancy: median absolute Spearman across the 24 index/view pairs <0.85 for each breadth role
representation_gate.breadth_role_conditional_distinctness: median absolute partial rank correlation between discovery and concentration after direction <0.85
representation_gate.coverage: all 24 index/view pairs and every 2019-2023 year represented
representation_gate.state_cell_rule: report sparse cells; do not merge, optimize, or remove them
